data.narrative:
Hystar, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Alejandro Oyarce Barnett, has raised $36M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 private and 1 public comparable—including KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C)—alongside broader reference to companies like Redwood Materials and QuantumScape operating in adjacent sectors.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling, using a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implies a $68M valuation from the $36M raised base. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same-or-adjacent-stage comparables yields a $1.0B midpoint, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. The peer-median method carries material weight given the specificity of comparable staging and sector alignment, though the wide peer range ($700M–$3.0B) reflects heterogeneity in market positioning and de-risking among Series C-stage peers.

Triangulation of these two methods supports a valuation range of $58M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median estimate of $534M. Key uncertainties include the appropriate stage discount relative to Series C comparables and whether Hystar's specific technology risk and market traction justify positioning toward the peer median or toward the stage-progression floor. Further diligence on capital efficiency and commercial-stage progress would sharpen this range.
